I'll start by reading TASK.md and brief.md so I can follow the brief exactly.Section 0 points at the T9b decision and the last T9b run. I'll read those completely before any experiment.The T9b record leaves the refresh trigger and the getter-to-geometry path open. I'll read the runners and the listings those trials used before designing version 1.The frame routine has no direct caller, so I’ll scan the image for its pointer and the dirty-byte readers before spending an emulator version.The only image pointer to the frame routine is in a handler table, and the setter’s other effect is the dirty byte. Version 1 will record the call stack on the post-setter idle, then force that getter return without writing the cell.The getter return is the causal input: with the cell left at 526, forcing that call to return 412 moved the marks. Next I’ll separate zone from position and find who writes the 406 geometry word.The cell write moved the marks, but nothing stored the geometry word at the address I watched, and the zone dial also moved the position. I’ll read the writer formula and the watchpoint path before spending the next emulator run.The pixel formula now fits every measured frame, including the centre. Next I’ll install the one display change and run the three validation versions.Version 4 measured the AF-ON frame, and the two controls passed. The pre-registered rectangles in version 4 did not match those measurements, so that run did not end clean. I’ll record that and seal the evidence.The getter return at `0x6041935b` is a causal input of the AF frame, and the one display change is in place. Version 4 did not pass its own pre-registered rectangles.

With `0x88b2` left at 526, forcing that call to return 412 moved the four marks to the 412 frame. The function `0x61184dd6` is entered by `calls (A2)` at `0x610c8b66` (vtable + `0x190`). A plain idle enters it. The dirty byte is not what schedules it. The two calls through `0x610cd5ac` only gate the writer.

The word at object + `0x364` is that return, except when the return modulo 39 is 22, in which case the word is the return minus 6. It is divided by 39. Mode 2 selects size constants 3 and 3. The corner glyphs are 19×21. Half-press All removes the 444 grey pixels.

While the owner byte is 2, that same call returns the current bank's mirror position and zone. `0xFFFF` passes through. Each edge then idles so the dispatch runs. On the seeded run, AF-ON draws (356, 265), (402, 265), (356, 314) and (402, 314), the Small ten-byte, owner 2, cell still 526. Owner 0 and S1 draw no grey marks. The unseeded control and stock both passed: the hook substitutes nothing when the mirror is `0xFF`, and stock stays on the centre frame.

Version 4 expected the centre box on the half-press edges and the uncorrected 529 box on AF-ON. The screenshots show the cleared All frame and the corrected 523 frame, so that run's final flag is a failure. The store that writes object + `0x364` was not captured. Six emulator processes were used.

`work/result.md` and `work/evidence-manifest.json` are in place, with the T9b corrections in `work/result-addendum-t9c.md` and the external seal at `work/out/seal-t9c.json`.The six emulator runs are finished and the records are in place.

The getter return at `0x6041935b` moves the AF marks while `0x88b2` stays 526. The frame function is entered by the idle call at `0x610c8b66`. With the owner byte at 2, that same call returns the mirror position. On AF-ON the seeded run draws (356, 265), (402, 265), (356, 314) and (402, 314). The half-press All frame has no grey marks. The unseeded control and stock both passed.

Version 4 exited 1 because its script expected the centre box and the uncorrected 529 box. The screenshots show the cleared All frame and the corrected 523 frame. That mismatch is recorded in `work/result.md`. `work/evidence-manifest.json` and `work/out/seal-t9c.json` are written.
